page: Amazon Web Services c7i-flex.12xlarge is a compute-optimized x86_64 server powered by custom 4th Generation Intel Xeon Scalable processors (Intel Xeon 8488C) operating at a 3.2 GHz clock speed. Built on the AWS Nitro System hypervisor, the instance provides 24 physical cores yielding 48 dedicated vCPUs with 2 threads per core. System memory consists of 96.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 RAM running at 5 GHz, maintaining a 2.0 GB memory-to-vCPU ratio. The processor architecture includes 105 MB of L3 cache alongside vector and matrix instruction extensions such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX (tile, int8, bf16). The instance features no local ephemeral storage and relies on EBS volumes, supported by 9 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth.

In benchmark testing, the instance exhibits strong performance across vector calculations, software compilation, and in-memory data processing. PassMark CPU evaluations record extended instruction scores of 66337.72 and encryption scores of 52712.57, backed by memory bandwidth reaching 222.1 GB/sec on uncached large-block reads. Web serving and caching workloads achieve high throughput, recording 72.85 GB/sec in static web serving benchmarks and 62.18 million operations per second in Redis SET tests. For machine learning tasks, LLM inference benchmarks place small model text generation (135M parameters) in the top tier at 353.0 tokens per second, alongside strong prompt processing throughput across medium and large models.

The hardware configuration provides high compute density for compute-bound applications, continuous integration build servers, web application backends, in-memory caches, and CPU-based artificial intelligence inference tasks. The presence of Intel AMX hardware accelerators enables efficient execution of matrix math operations without requiring dedicated discrete GPUs.
